newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates steady on spinners demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates steady on spinners demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed steady on Saturday as demand remained higher than supply and dealers said they expected the prices to move in a narrow range in the near term.
"Until bulk supply of cotton starts from the Punjab province, the prices will retain these levels," dealer Kishan Chand said. "At present the demand is higher than the supply."
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety from the 1996/97 crop was traded at 2,400 rupees ($67.22) per maund (37.32 kg) and the MNH-93 at 2,450 rupees, dealers said.
The Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said customs-cleared cotton exports had reached 1,824,676 375-lb bales by July 31, since the 1995/96 picking season began on September 1.
Imports had reached 47,545 480-lb bales in the same period.
